title: Pahoran’s letter arrives
summary: Moroni receives an epistle from Pahoran, who writes that Moroni’s afflictions grieve him.

explicit_facts.text: Soon after Moroni sent an epistle to the chief governor, he received an epistle from Pahoran.
Pahoran identifies himself as chief governor and Moroni as chief captain over the army.
Pahoran says Moroni’s afflictions grieve his soul.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Moroni can be shown receiving and reading a letter.
unspecified_visual_details: The place where Moroni receives the letter, its appearance, and who delivers it are not stated.

narration.text: he received an epistle from Pahoran
it grieves my soul

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Pahoran as physically present; the verses present his words as a letter.

title: Rebellion and withheld support
summary: Pahoran explains in his letter that numerous rebels oppose him, have sought his judgment-seat, withheld provisions, and daunted freemen from coming to Moroni.

explicit_facts.text: Numerous people have rebelled against Pahoran and freemen.
Those seeking to take Pahoran’s judgment-seat used flattery to lead away many people.
The rebels withheld provisions and daunted freemen from going to Moroni.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The letter may be shown as off-screen narration over a neutral setting.
unspecified_visual_details: No present action or specific setting for these reported events is established.

narration.text: they have risen up in rebellion against me
they have withheld our provisions

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These events are reported in a letter, not narrated as occurring in the present.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage the reported flattery, withholding, or rebellion as a new present-tense event.

title: Pahoran flees to Gideon
summary: Pahoran reports that he was driven out and fled to the land of Gideon with as many men as he could gather.

explicit_facts.text: Pahoran was driven out and fled to the land of Gideon with as many men as he could get.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The flight may be represented as a past event within the letter, using a restrained visual treatment.
unspecified_visual_details: The route, landscape, number of men, and their appearance are not stated.

narration.text: I have fled to the land of Gideon

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The flight is reported retrospectively in the letter.
prohibited_inventions: Do not add pursuit, combat, or details about the flight.

title: Freemen rally to Pahoran
summary: Pahoran says his proclamation has drawn people daily to arm themselves in defense of their country and freedom; the rebels now fear to come out to battle.

explicit_facts.text: Pahoran sent a proclamation throughout part of the land, and people flocked to him daily with arms.
The people came to defend their country and freedom and avenge their wrongs.
The rebels feared Pahoran’s people and did not dare come out against them to battle.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A gathering of armed people is supported by the report.
unspecified_visual_details: The location and appearance of the gathering and the people are not specified.

narration.text: they are flocking to us daily
they do fear us

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The events are reported in the letter.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show a battle; the letter says the rebels did not come out to battle.

title: The rebels hold Zarahemla
summary: Pahoran reports that the rebels possess Zarahemla, appointed a king, and allied with the Lamanite king in a plan tied to the conquest of the land.

explicit_facts.text: The rebels possess the land or city of Zarahemla and appointed a king over themselves.
Their appointed king wrote to the king of the Lamanites and formed an alliance.
The alliance concerns maintaining Zarahemla for the Lamanites’ hoped-for conquest; the appointed king expects to rule after the conquest.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Zarahemla may be shown as held by the rebels.
unspecified_visual_details: The appointed king’s identity and appearance, the letter exchange, and the alliance’s visual specifics are unstated.

narration.text: They have got possession of the land, or the city, of Zarahemla

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The proposed future conquest is an expectation described in the letter, not an event that occurs in this chapter.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Lamanite conquest or give the appointed king an invented identity.

title: Pahoran’s purpose
summary: Pahoran says he is not angry about the censure in the addressee’s epistle. He says he seeks to retain his judgment-seat to preserve his people’s rights and liberty.

explicit_facts.text: Pahoran says the addressee censured him in an epistle.
Pahoran says he is not angry and rejoices in the greatness of the addressee’s heart.
Pahoran says he seeks to retain his judgment-seat to preserve his people’s rights and liberty.
Pahoran says his soul stands fast in the liberty in which God made them free.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The words may be presented as text without depicting a physical exchange.
unspecified_visual_details: Pahoran’s appearance and location are not specified.

narration.text: I am not angry, but do rejoice in the greatness of your heart.
I, Pahoran, do not seek for power, save only to retain my judgment-seat that I may preserve the rights and the liberty of my people.

prohibited_inventions: Do not identify the addressee by name from this verse.
Do not depict a physical letter exchange or invent Pahoran’s appearance or location.

title: Resisting wickedness
summary: Pahoran writes that they will resist wickedness, while saying they would not shed Lamanite or fellow-citizen blood if those groups did not take hostile action.

explicit_facts.text: Pahoran says they will resist wickedness even unto bloodshed.
He says they would not shed Lamanite blood if the Lamanites stayed in their own land.
He says they would not shed their brethren’s blood if they did not rebel and take the sword against them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The letter can be presented as off-screen narration without depicting combat.
unspecified_visual_details: No combat occurs in these verses; the conditional statements do not establish a specific battle.

narration.text: we will resist wickedness even unto bloodshed
We would not shed the blood of our brethren

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These are conditional and principled statements, not accounts of a particular act of violence.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict bloodshed or a battle as occurring.

title: Trust in God
summary: Pahoran says they would accept bondage if justice or God required it, but God does not command them to submit to their enemies and they should trust in him for deliverance.

explicit_facts.text: Pahoran says they would subject themselves to bondage if justice required it or God commanded it.
He says God does not command them to submit to their enemies, but to trust in him, and that he will deliver them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Use the letter as off-screen narration rather than depicting bondage or divine intervention.
unspecified_visual_details: No visible divine appearance or deliverance is described.

narration.text: put our trust in him
he will deliver us

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The promised deliverance is expressed as teaching and assurance, not a narrated visible miracle.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict God, bondage, or a deliverance event.

title: Resist evil
summary: Pahoran urges Moroni to resist evil with words where possible and with swords against rebellions and dissensions, to retain freedom and serve their church and Redeemer.

explicit_facts.text: Pahoran urges Moroni to resist evil and use swords against rebellions and dissensions that words cannot resist.
He gives retaining freedom and rejoicing in their church and the cause of their Redeemer and God as purposes.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The letter may be shown with its words narrated off-screen.
unspecified_visual_details: No particular sword-bearing action or confrontation is narrated.

narration.text: let us resist evil
that we may retain our freedom

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The instruction to use swords is counsel, not an event occurring in the scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage a battle or show a specific act of violence.

title: Moroni summoned
summary: Pahoran asks Moroni to come quickly with a few men, leave the rest under Lehi and Teancum, and notes that he has sent provisions to them.

explicit_facts.text: Pahoran asks Moroni to come to him quickly with a few men.
He asks Moroni to leave the remainder under Lehi and Teancum, empowered to conduct the war in that part of the land.
Pahoran says he sent provisions to Lehi and Teancum so they would not perish before Moroni could come.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The letter may be shown as off-screen narration; no arrival or delivery of provisions is shown as occurring now.
unspecified_visual_details: The men’s identities beyond those named, provisions, and locations are not specified.

narration.text: come unto me speedily with a few of your men
I have sent a few provisions unto them

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These are requests and a report of prior provisions, not completed actions by Moroni.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Moroni obeying the request or the provisions arriving.

title: Plan to retake Zarahemla
summary: Pahoran proposes gathering forces on Moroni’s march, going against the dissenters, and taking Zarahemla to obtain more food for Lehi and Teancum.

explicit_facts.text: Pahoran asks Moroni to gather whatever force he can while marching to him.
Pahoran proposes going against the dissenters in God’s strength.
He says they will take Zarahemla to obtain more food for Lehi and Teancum and put an end to the iniquity.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The letter may continue as off-screen narration.
unspecified_visual_details: The proposed march, battle, and taking of Zarahemla are not shown as completed events.

narration.text: we will go speedily against those dissenters
we will take possession of the city of Zarahemla

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These are plans and intentions, not events that occur in this chapter.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the proposed march, fighting, or capture of Zarahemla.

title: Pahoran closes his letter
summary: Pahoran rejoices at Moroni’s letter, recalls his concern about going against their brethren, acknowledges Moroni’s instruction, and closes with counsel to strengthen Lehi and Teancum and not fear.

explicit_facts.text: Pahoran rejoices to receive Moroni’s letter and says he had worried whether going against their brethren was just.
Pahoran says Moroni wrote that the Lord commanded him to go against them unless they repent.
Pahoran asks Moroni to strengthen Lehi and Teancum in the Lord and tell them not to fear.
Pahoran says God will deliver those who stand fast in the liberty with which God made them free, then closes the epistle to Moroni.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The closing lines may be narrated over the letter without showing Pahoran physically.
unspecified_visual_details: Pahoran’s location and appearance are not specified.

narration.text: I do joy in receiving your epistle
I close mine epistle to my beloved brother, Moroni

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The command and deliverance are reported or stated in the letter; no divine figure appears.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Lord speaking or show a deliverance event.
